title: UGC NET English Paper II — December 2012
subject: English

questions.question: Identify the work below that does not belong to the literature of the eighteenth century :
questions.explanation: Bacon's The Advancement of Learning appeared in 1605; the other three works belong to the eighteenth century.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: Which, among the following, is a place through which John Bunyan's Christian does NOT pass?
questions.explanation: Mount Helicon is not among the places Christian visits in The Pilgrim's Progress.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: The period of Queen Victoria's reign is
questions.explanation: Queen Victoria reigned from 1837 to 1901.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Lyrical Ballads is NOT true?
options: It carried only one ballad proper, which was Coleridge's The Rime of the Ancient Mariner.
It also carried pastoral and other poems.
It carried a "Preface" which Wordsworth added in 1800.
It also printed from Gray's Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard.
questions.explanation: Gray's Elegy was not printed in Lyrical Ballads.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: One of the following texts was published earlier than 1955. Identify the text :
questions.explanation: Waiting for Godot appeared before 1955, making it the answer recorded in the updated UGC key.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: Who among the poets in England during the 1930s had left-leaning tendencies?
options: T.S. Eliot, Ezra Pound, Richard Aldington
Wilfred Owen, Siegfried Sassoon, Rupert Brooke
W.H. Auden, Louis MacNeice, Cecil Day Lewis
J. Fleckner, W.H. Davies, Edward Marsh
questions.explanation: Auden, MacNeice and Day-Lewis were associated with left-wing politics in the 1930s.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question:
Match the following:
1. The Sage of Concord
2. The Nun of Amherst
3. Mark Twain
4. Old Possum
5. Emily Dickinson
6. R. W. Emerson
7. T. S. Eliot
8. Samuel L. Clemens
questions.explanation: Emerson was the Sage of Concord, Dickinson the Nun of Amherst, Mark Twain was Samuel L. Clemens, and Old Possum was T. S. Eliot.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: Name the theorist who divided poets into "strong" and "weak" and popularized the practice of misreading:
questions.explanation: Harold Bloom used the terms strong and weak poets and developed the account of poetic misreading.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: In The Rape of the Lock Pope repeatedly compares Belinda to
questions.explanation: Belinda is repeatedly compared to the sun in The Rape of the Lock.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: Which of the following awards is not given to Indian-English writers?
questions.explanation: The updated UGC answer key accepts both (c) and (d) for this question. This test counts (c), the Gyanpeeth (Jnanpith) Award: when this paper was set in December 2012, no writer in English had won it. Amitav Ghosh became the first, with the award for 2018.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: Identify the correct statement below :
options: Gorboduc is a comedy, while Ralph Roister Doister and Gammer Gurton's Needle are tragedies.
Gorboduc is a tragedy, while Ralph Roister Doister and Gammer Gurton's Needle are comedies.
all of them are problem plays.
questions.explanation: Gorboduc is a tragedy; Ralph Roister Doister and Gammer Gurton's Needle are comedies.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: W.M. Thackeray's Vanity Fair owes its title to
questions.explanation: Thackeray's Vanity Fair takes its title from the fair in Bunyan's The Pilgrim's Progress.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: The Puritans shut down all theaters in England in
questions.explanation: Parliament ordered the closure of English theatres in 1642.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: Who of the following was not a contemporary of Wordsworth and Coleridge?
questions.explanation: Swinburne belongs to the Victorian generation, later than Wordsworth and Coleridge.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about Waiting for Godot is true?
1. It carries a subtitle: "a tragicomedy in two acts"
2. It carries a subtitle: "a tragicomedy in two scenes"
3. It carries a subtitle: "a tragicomedy in two parts"
4. It does not carry a subtitle.
questions.explanation: Beckett's English version carries the subtitle "a tragicomedy in two acts", which is statement 1 (the last option). The updated UGC key gave marks to every candidate for this item; this test counts that option.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question:
The Bloomsbury Group included British intellectuals, critics, writers and artists. Who among the following belonged to the Bloomsbury Group?
I. John Maynard Keynes, Lytton Strachey
II. E.M. Forster, Roger Fry, Clive Bell
III. Patrick Brunty, Paul Haworth
IV. Thomas Hardy, Henry James, Walter Pater
questions.explanation: Keynes, Strachey, Forster, Fry and Bell were members of the Bloomsbury Group.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: Who among the following is credited with the making of the first authoritative Dictionary of the English Language?
questions.explanation: Samuel Johnson published A Dictionary of the English Language in 1755.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: In Dryden's Essay of Dramatic Poesy (1668), who opens the discussion on behalf of the ancients?
questions.explanation: Crites speaks for the ancients in Dryden's An Essay of Dramatic Poesy.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: The term 'invective' refers to
options: the abusive writing or speech in which there is harsh denunciation of some person or thing.
an insulting writing attack upon a real person, in verse or prose, usually involving caricature and ridicule.
a written or spoken text in which an apparently straightforward statement or event is undermined in its context so as to give it a very different significance.
the chanting or reciting of words deemed to have magical power.
questions.explanation: Invective is abusive speech or writing directed against someone or something.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: Which of the following novels depicts the plight of the Bangladeshi immigrants in East London?
questions.explanation: Monica Ali's Brick Lane centres on Bangladeshi immigrant life in East London.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: The year 1939 proved to be a crucial year for two important writers in England. Identify the correct phrase below :
options: For Yeats who died, for Auden who left England for the U.S.
For Eliot who started publishing verse- drama, for Hardy, whose 'Wessex Poems' were published.
For Evelyn Waugh and Graham Greene, each for publishing his first novels.
For Eliot who won the Nobel Prize and Orwell who published his 'Animal Farm'.
questions.explanation: W. B. Yeats died in 1939, the year W. H. Auden moved to the United States.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: The Enlightenment was characterized by
options: accelerated industrial production and general well-being of the public.
a belief in the universal authority of reason and emphasis on scientific experimentation.
the Protestant work ethic and compliance with Christian values of life.
an undue faith in predestination and neglect of free will.
questions.explanation: The Enlightenment stressed reason and scientific inquiry.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: Which Shakespearean play contains the line: " ....... there is a special providence in the fall of a sparrow"?
questions.explanation: Hamlet says this to Horatio before the duel with Laertes.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question:
Match the following pairs of books and authors:
I. Condition of the Working Class in England
II. London Labour and the London Poor
III. Past and Present
IV. Unto This Last
i. John Ruskin
ii. Henry Mayhew
iii. Thomas Carlyle
iv. Friedrich Engels
Codes: I II III IV
questions.explanation: The correct matching is Engels, Mayhew, Carlyle and Ruskin, in that order.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: In which of the following texts do Aston, Davies and Mick appear as characters?
options: Katherine Mansfield's Life of Ma Parker
questions.explanation: Aston, Davies and Mick are characters in Pinter's The Caretaker.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question:
What is common to the following writers? Identify the correct description below:
William Congreve
George Etherege
William Wycherley
Thomas Otway
options: All of these were Restoration play-wrights
All of them were critics of Orwell's regime
All of them edited Shakespeare's plays
All of them wrote tragedies in the same age
questions.explanation: Congreve, Etherege, Wycherley and Otway were Restoration playwrights.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: In which Jane Austen novel do you find the characters Anne Elliott, Lady Russell, Louisa Musgrove and Captain Wentworth?
questions.explanation: Anne Elliot, Lady Russell, Louisa Musgrove and Captain Wentworth appear in Persuasion.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: In which of his essays does Homi Bhabha discuss the 'discovery' of English in colonial India?
questions.explanation: Bhabha discusses the colonial introduction of English in 'Signs Taken for Wonders'.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: .........was The first Sonnet Sequence in English.
questions.explanation: Sidney's Astrophel and Stella is the sequence identified by the updated UGC key.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: Which is the correct sequence of the novels of V.S. Naipaul?
options: The Mystic Masseur- Miguel Street- The Suffrage of Elvira- A House for Mr. Biswas.
Miguel Street- The Mystic Masseur- A House for Mr. Biswas- The Suffrage of Elvira.
The Suffrage of Elvira- Miguel Street- The Mystic Masseur- A House for Mr. Biswas.
The Mystic Masseur- The Suffrage of Elvira- Miguel Street- A House for Mr. Biswas.
questions.explanation: The listed publication order is The Mystic Masseur, The Suffrage of Elvira, Miguel Street and A House for Mr Biswas.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: "Kubla Khan" takes an epigraph from
questions.explanation: The epigraph to 'Kubla Khan' draws on Samuel Purchas's Purchas His Pilgrimage.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: Which of the following author-theme is correctly matched? Author Theme
options: 'The Battle of the Books' (J. Swift) Quarrel between ancient and modern authors.
'The Rape of the Lock' (A. Pope) Tribute to "The rude forefathers of the hamlet".
Gray's "Elegy" Accumulation of wealth and loss of human lives and values.
'The Deserted Village' (Oliver Goldsmith) Quarrel between two families caused by Lord Peter.
questions.explanation: Only the first pairing is correct: Swift's The Battle of the Books is a satire on the quarrel between ancient and modern authors. The other three pairings mix up works and themes. The updated UGC key gave marks to every candidate for this item; this test counts the first option.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: Which among the following titles set a course for academic literary feminism?
options: A Dance to the Music of Time
questions.explanation: Virginia Woolf's A Room of One's Own became a foundational text of academic literary feminism.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: In which play do we see a reworking of E.M. Forster's A Passage to India as a cameo?
questions.explanation: Tom Stoppard's Indian Ink includes a cameo reworking of A Passage to India.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: Shakespeare's sonnets
options: are dedicated to James I of England.
are dedicated to an unknown "Mr. W.H."
questions.explanation: The dedication in the 1609 edition of Shakespeare's sonnets addresses 'Mr. W. H.'; his identity is uncertain.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: Which of the following poems uses terza rima?
options: P.B. Shelley's "Ode to the West Wind"
questions.explanation: Shelley's 'Ode to the West Wind' uses interlocking terza rima rhymes.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: When one says that "someone is no more" or that "someone has breathed his/her last", The speaker is resorting to
questions.explanation: A euphemism uses a milder expression for a potentially harsh one.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: Which of the following are "companion poems"?
options: "Full Fathom Five" and "Hark, Hark! the Lark"
questions.explanation: Milton's 'L'Allegro' and 'Il Penseroso' are companion poems contrasting states of mind.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: What does the term 'episteme' signify?
questions.explanation: Episteme is a Greek term for knowledge.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: Which of the following is a better definition of an image in literary writing?
questions.explanation: 'A speaking picture' is the option selected in the updated UGC key.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: Whom did Keats regard as the prime example of 'negative capability'?
questions.explanation: Keats held Shakespeare up as an example of negative capability.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: Charles Dickens's A Tale of Two Cities begins with the sentence
options: It was the best of times, it was the worst of times.
It was the brightest of times, it was the darkest of times.
It was the richest of times, it was the poorest of times.
It was the happiest of times, it was the saddest of times.
questions.explanation: The novel opens, 'It was the best of times, it was the worst of times.'
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: The works of Gerard Manley Hopkins were published posthumously by
questions.explanation: Robert Bridges edited Hopkins's poems for posthumous publication.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct chronological sequence?
options: A Poison Tree - The Deserted Village - The Blessed Damozel - Ozymandias
The Deserted Village - A Poison Tree - Ozymandias - The Blessed Damozel
The Blessed Damozel - A Poison Tree - The Deserted Village - Ozymandias
The Deserted Village - The Blessed Damozel - Ozymandias - A Poison Tree
questions.explanation: The order is The Deserted Village (1770), 'A Poison Tree' (1794), 'Ozymandias' (1818), and 'The Blessed Damozel' (1850).
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: The term homology means a correspondence between two or more structures. Who of the following developed a theory of relations between literary works and social classes in terms of homologies?
questions.explanation: The updated UGC answer key accepts either (a) Raymond Williams or (c) Lucien Goldmann. This test counts (c): Goldmann's genetic structuralism rests on homologies between the structure of a literary work and the mental structure of a social group.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: F. Turner's famous hypothesis is that
options: the Frontier has outlived its ideological utility in American civilization.
the Frontier has posed a challenge to the American creative imagination
the Frontier has been the one great determinant of American civilization
the frontier has been the one great deterrent to American progress.
questions.explanation: Frederick Jackson Turner's frontier thesis treats the frontier as a major force shaping American civilization.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question:
Which statement(s) below on the Spenserian Stanza is/are accurate?
I. a quatrain, unrhymed, but alliterative
II. a stanza of four lines in iambic pentameter
III. an eight-line stanza in iambic pentameter followed by a ninth in six iambic feet
IV. an eight-line stanza with six iambic feet followed by a ninth in iambic pentameter
questions.explanation: A Spenserian stanza has eight pentameter lines followed by a ninth alexandrine line.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question:
Match the following texts with their respective themes:
I. Areopagitica (Milton)
II. Leviathan (Hobbes)
III. Alexander's Feast (Dryden)
IV. The Way of the World (Congreve)
i. Fashion, courtship, seduction
ii. The liberty for unlicensed printing
iii. Absolute sovereignty
iv. The power of music
Codes: I II III IV
questions.explanation: The pairings are Areopagitica—unlicensed printing, Leviathan—sovereignty, Alexander's Feast—music, and The Way of the World—fashion and courtship.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question: The preliminary version of James Joyce's Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man was called
options: A Day in the life of Stephen Dedalus
questions.explanation: Joyce's earlier version of A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man was Stephen Hero.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012

questions.question:
(i) A pastiche is a mixture of themes, stylistic elements of subjects borrowed from other works.
(ii) It is distinguished from parody because not all parody is pastiche.
(iii) A pastiche is also known as a 'purple passage'.
(iv) A pastiche is given to an elevated style, especially in its use of figurative language.
questions.explanation: The updated UGC key selects statements (i) and (ii) about pastiche.
questions.src: UGC NET English Paper II, December 2012
